claims.statement: Absolute risk reduction is the comparator risk minus intervention risk, and number needed to treat is the reciprocal of that absolute difference with outcome and time horizon stated.

claims.statement: A p-value is the probability, under a specified null model, of data at least as incompatible with that model as the observed data; it is not the probability that the null is true.

claims.statement: Type I error is rejection under a true null, type II error is failure to reject under a specified alternative, and power is the probability of rejection under that alternative.

claims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

claims.limitation: Composition/volume prescription priority and named whey/glucose-polymer module examples extend the screening/route atoms. Verify the exact proposed substitution with dietetic guidance; fictional observed intake is not a universal target threshold. Offline author synthesis, not external verification; original source dates are unchanged. Named clinician review required.
claims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly bounded fictional N2 round-three record; no empirical rate, medication dose, washout period or universal clinical cutoff.

claims.statement: Recurrence after one deliberately limited balloon session does not by itself establish failure of a completed endoscopic treatment strategy for a gastrojejunal narrowing.
claims.limitation: Verify the repeat-dilation priority and the actual suitability boundaries for stent and operation in the recorded bariatric guidance; no session count or diameter rule is inferred. Offline author synthesis, not external verification; original source dates are unchanged. Named clinician review required.
claims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly bounded fictional N2 round-three record; no empirical rate, medication dose, washout period or universal clinical cutoff.

claims.statement: When metabolic deterioration follows intravenous carbohydrate before enteral formula delivery, reassessment of the carbohydrate prescription must include the intravenous source rather than change the formula route in isolation.
claims.limitation: Exposure recognition is recorded, but the exact reduce-versus-advance management ranking is not. Verify it against permitted refeeding guidance, preserving disagreements and avoiding a universal phosphate trigger. Offline author synthesis, not external verification; original source dates are unchanged. Named clinician review required.
claims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly bounded fictional N2 round-three record; no empirical rate, medication dose, washout period or universal clinical cutoff.

claims.statement: In the constructed stabilized rebleeding course after initial successful ulcer hemostasis, a repeat endoscopic attempt precedes the represented catheter or operative rescue options.
claims.limitation: Repeat endoscopy is recorded; the precise priority over embolization/operation and the chosen stabilization context need direct verification. Offline author synthesis, not external verification; original source dates are unchanged. Named clinician review required.
claims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly bounded fictional N2 round-three record; no empirical rate, medication dose, washout period or universal clinical cutoff.

claims.statement: A rapidly changing renal course and a pending invasive procedure can favor intravenous unfractionated heparin as an initially titratable therapeutic anticoagulant for acute venous thrombosis.
claims.limitation: Initial-agent priority and alternatives in evolving renal injury are not established by the recorded duration/purpose atoms. Verify UFH, adjusted enoxaparin and apixaban comparisons and ordinary eligibility requirements. Offline author synthesis, not external verification; original source dates are unchanged. Named clinician review required.
claims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly bounded fictional N2 round-three record; no empirical rate, medication dose, washout period or universal clinical cutoff.

claims.statement: Opioid exposure can accompany an achalasia-like spastic pattern, and assessment off opioids is advised when feasible.
claims.limitation: Conditional, low-grade consensus guidance. Withdrawal must be coordinated; no abrupt cessation, fixed washout or universal reversibility is claimed. Unchanged recorded statement; original last-check date retained. Exact new application and currentness unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

claims.statement: Recurrent peptic-ulcer bleeding after initial successful hemostasis can warrant repeat endoscopic therapy, with consideration of an OTS clip.
claims.limitation: One adequate current full primary guideline. Actual resuscitation/access and prior course matter; not a universal requirement to repeat endoscopy despite any instability or contraindication. Unchanged recorded statement; original last-check date retained. Exact new application and currentness unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: The identified synthetic adult clinical or employee teaching cases; observed values are constructed case inputs, not empirical patient/gameplay data.

claims.statement: A suspicious anal-canal lesion requires tissue biopsy to establish SCC; CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis plus pelvic MRI can stage disease when included in the same referral.
claims.limitation: No biopsy technique or unrequested imaging result is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable patients with a suspicious anal-canal lesion.

claims.statement: For nonmetastatic anal-canal SCC after biopsy, CT, and pelvic MRI, referral for definitive chemoradiation is the broad management path.
claims.limitation: Excludes small perianal-margin lesions and treatment regimen details.
claims.applicablePopulation: Appropriately staged, nonmetastatic anal-canal SCC.

claims.statement: Fever in a person with impaired splenic function requires immediate emergency assessment; a patient-specific standby oral antibiotic plan does not replace emergency presentation or prompt parenteral treatment after evaluation.
claims.limitation: The case does not select a drug, dose, diagnosis, or outpatient test pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Known asplenic adults with new fever.

claims.statement: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis should be discontinued after incision closure; continuing it solely because a drain remains does not reduce surgical-site infection and adds antimicrobial harms.
claims.limitation: This concerns prophylaxis only, not treatment for an established infection or another therapeutic indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Postoperative adults with a closed incision, no established infection, and a prophylactic antibiotic continued solely because a drain remains.

claims.statement: Stable follow-up for persistently increased ileostomy output warrants assessment of renal function, electrolytes, and magnesium for fluid and salt depletion.
claims.limitation: This outpatient pathway excludes shock, acute kidney injury, infection, and obstruction and does not define a universal output threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistently increased watery ileostomy losses and no acute complication.

claims.statement: After stabilization, a sodium-glucose oral rehydration plan is preferred to simply increasing hypotonic plain-water intake for high-output ileostomy losses.
claims.limitation: No exact output threshold, oral-rehydration formulation, total fluid target, or medication regimen is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with high-output ileostomy losses who can drink and have no acute kidney injury, shock, infection, or obstruction.

claims.statement: For postoperative inability to void, bladder scanning provides an objective assessment before selecting a retention intervention.
claims.limitation: No numeric scan threshold is taught, and suspected urethral trauma requires a different evaluation pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults who cannot void and have no evidence of urethral trauma.

claims.statement: Clearly symptomatic postoperative urinary retention with a large retained bladder volume warrants catheter decompression.
claims.limitation: The claim does not set a universal volume threshold or choose between intermittent and indwelling catheterization for every patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults with symptoms and a bladder scan showing a large retained volume without urethral trauma.

claims.statement: Before a management-changing biopsy of an indeterminate adrenal mass, pheochromocytoma should be excluded with plasma-free or urinary fractionated metanephrines; adrenal biopsy is otherwise rarely appropriate.
claims.limitation: This is restricted to imaging not typical of a benign adenoma and a specific situation in which tissue would change management. It does not teach routine adrenal biopsy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an indeterminate adrenal lesion and a separate malignancy for which biopsy could change treatment.

claims.statement: Symptomatic fibrostenotic eosinophilic esophagitis can require esophageal dilation for narrowing together with anti-inflammatory treatment for the underlying disease.
claims.limitation: Dilation does not replace anti-inflammatory care. Several anti-inflammatory strategies can be valid, so the game does not force a single medication or diet.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with biopsy-supported eosinophilic esophagitis and a symptomatic fixed narrowing or fibrostenotic phenotype.

claims.statement: Suspected eosinophilic esophagitis should be evaluated by upper endoscopy with at least six targeted esophageal biopsies obtained from at least two levels, interpreted with symptoms and exclusion of other causes.
claims.limitation: Endoscopic appearance alone is insufficient. The authored patient has no current food impaction or unstable illness.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with chronic solid-food dysphagia or food sticking suspicious for eosinophilic esophagitis.

claims.statement: Endoanal ultrasound is a selected anatomy study when sphincter repair is being considered after appropriate evaluation for persistent fecal incontinence.
claims.limitation: A sphincter defect alone does not predict symptom severity or mandate an operation. Ultrasound is not a routine test for every patient with fecal incontinence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with persistent fecal incontinence for whom specialist evaluation has identified possible sphincter injury and repair planning is under consideration.

claims.statement: Dietary and medical measures that improve bowel habits and stool consistency are first-line care for stable fecal incontinence.
claims.limitation: No single diet, medication, dose, or regimen is universally appropriate; care should respond to the patient's stool pattern and contributors.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults presenting for initial management of fecal incontinence without an acute neurologic, infectious, or obstructive feature.

claims.statement: A suitable patient with recent symptoms and severe 70–99% ipsilateral carotid stenosis should receive prompt assessment for carotid endarterectomy together with best medical therapy.
claims.limitation: This excludes near-occlusion, complete occlusion, large infarct, hemorrhage, disabling deficit, prohibitive anatomy, and unsuitable operative risk.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable suitable adults with recent ipsilateral symptoms and confirmed severe carotid stenosis after completed acute stroke assessment.

claims.statement: CTA is the principal anatomic diagnostic study for suspected occlusive chronic mesenteric ischemia after compatible symptoms and reasonable evaluation for alternative causes.
claims.limitation: Excludes acute mesenteric ischemia, nonocclusive disease, and patients who cannot receive iodinated contrast; no exact stenosis threshold is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with chronic postprandial pain, reduced intake or weight loss, atherosclerotic risk, and no acute-abdomen features.

claims.statement: Compatible symptoms with significant celiac and superior mesenteric arterial disease support prompt expert vascular referral for revascularization planning without requiring a separate functional confirmation test.
claims.limitation: The concept does not choose open versus endovascular repair, a device, or a target-vessel sequence; several recommendations rely on observational evidence and expert agreement.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with compatible symptoms and confirmed multivessel occlusive chronic mesenteric ischemia after alternative GI causes have been evaluated.

claims.statement: Poor differentiation and perineural invasion are high-risk pathological features in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; their absence in a shallow well-differentiated primary supports the constrained low-risk teaching case.
claims.limitation: Formal risk assessment uses multiple clinical and pathological features; this claim does not create a complete staging system.
claims.applicablePopulation: Localized pathology-confirmed cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma in the authored clinic cases.

claims.statement: Standard excision with histologic margin assessment is appropriate for low-risk primary cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, whereas high-risk disease should be evaluated for Mohs micrographic surgery.
claims.limitation: Risk classification must be explicit; location alone is not a universal Mohs indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with pathology-confirmed localized cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

claims.statement: Diabetes-related foot soft-tissue infection is diagnosed clinically from local or systemic inflammatory findings; colonization alone does not establish infection.
claims.limitation: Single-current-guideline limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with diabetes and a foot wound.

claims.statement: Systemic or local antibiotics should not be used for a clinically uninfected diabetic foot ulcer solely to prevent infection or promote healing.
claims.limitation: External multidisciplinary foot care remains required; no onsite wound service is implied.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a clinically uninfected diabetes-related foot ulcer.

claims.statement: After a first recovered complicated diverticulitis episode with abscess and no recent adequate examination, colonoscopy can be selected to exclude an alternative lesion.
claims.limitation: No exact interval is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable patients recovered from a first complicated left-sided diverticulitis episode without recent adequate colonoscopy.

claims.statement: For a recurrent high transsphincteric tract involving substantial external sphincter and no undrained abscess, loose seton drainage with staged sphincter-preserving planning avoids routine sphincter division.
claims.limitation: One guideline source; this is not a universal seton recommendation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable recurrent high transsphincteric cryptoglandular fistula without an undrained abscess.

claims.statement: ERCP can remove a stone lodged in the common bile duct; that indication is distinct from treating uncomplicated stones confined to the gallbladder.
claims.limitation: This supporting boundary does not define every indication for ERCP.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for gallstone disease where duct intervention is considered.

claims.statement: Incidentally found gallstones without symptoms or suspicious features usually do not require prophylactic surgery.
claims.limitation: Higher-risk gallbladder features and later biliary symptoms are outside this pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic adults with uncomplicated incidental gallstones.

claims.statement: Recurrent compatible symptoms with ultrasound-confirmed gallstones support elective surgical assessment and cholecystectomy counseling.
claims.limitation: Individual operative suitability and competing diagnoses still require assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with symptomatic gallstones and no acute complication in this encounter.

claims.statement: Initial eradication treatment must be followed by confirmation that H. pylori was eradicated and by endoscopic biopsy reassessment of lymphoma response rather than being treated as a one-time antibiotic prescription with no follow-up.
claims.limitation: Lymphoma regression can be delayed. Exact follow-up intervals and subsequent management depend on eradication status, pathology, symptoms, stage, and adverse features.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for gastric MALT lymphoma.

claims.statement: Gastric MALT lymphoma is recognized by an integrated pathologic pattern that includes a small B-cell infiltrate with gland-infiltrating lymphoepithelial lesions and a compatible immunophenotype, commonly CD20 positive with CD5, CD10, and cyclin D1 absent.
claims.limitation: CD20 establishes B-cell lineage but is not specific for MALT lymphoma. Diagnosis requires integrated morphology and immunophenotyping, with additional evaluation when a limited biopsy is equivocal.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing pathologic evaluation of a gastric lymphoid infiltrate obtained by endoscopic biopsy.

claims.statement: Large-cell transformation, clinically significant progression, threatening organ effects, or failure after an adequate eradication pathway requires reassessment and may require radiotherapy or systemic lymphoma treatment rather than repetition of an eradication-only strategy.
claims.limitation: This boundary does not assign one universal second-line treatment; subsequent therapy is individualized to stage, pathology, symptoms, prior response, and specialist assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastric MALT lymphoma outside the classic localized low-grade eradication-first presentation or with an inadequate response.

claims.statement: For an otherwise fit adult with uncomplicated appendicitis and an appendicolith, hospital surgical evaluation for appendectomy is favored over a routine antibiotics-only pathway.
claims.limitation: The SAGES recommendation for operative management is conditional, and patient circumstances and preferences still require shared decision-making.
claims.applicablePopulation: Otherwise fit adults with imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis containing an appendicolith.

claims.statement: Among adults choosing antibiotics for imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis, an appendicolith is associated with a greater chance of complications or later appendectomy than no appendicolith.
claims.limitation: This risk modifier informs shared decision-making and is not an absolute prohibition on nonoperative care.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis who are considering an antibiotics-first strategy.

claims.statement: When an adult with ARDS receives invasive ventilation, tidal-volume selection is based on predicted body weight rather than current actual body weight.
claims.limitation: The authored objective tests the weight basis only and does not prescribe a universal numeric tidal volume or reproduce a calculation formula.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with ARDS receiving invasive mechanical ventilation.

claims.statement: A new ECG abnormality after suspected blunt cardiac injury, or an elevated troponin despite a normal ECG, warrants admission to a monitored hospital setting.
claims.limitation: The guideline is from 2012, does not establish an optimal troponin timing schedule, and does not make every ECG abnormality diagnostic of structural cardiac injury.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated after blunt chest trauma concerning for blunt cardiac injury.

claims.statement: Adults with a mechanism concerning for blunt cardiac injury should undergo an admission ECG, and adding cardiac troponin improves the initial evaluation compared with ECG alone.
claims.limitation: The optimal timing and serial schedule for troponin testing remain uncertain, so no assay cutoff or testing interval is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with blunt chest trauma concerning for blunt cardiac injury.

claims.statement: When both the admission ECG and troponin I are normal after suspected blunt cardiac injury, blunt cardiac injury is ruled out for disposition purposes in the EAST pathway.
claims.limitation: This disposition principle does not override another injury, symptom, or clinical reason for hospital admission; exact diagnostic-performance percentages are not asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected blunt cardiac injury and normal admission ECG and troponin I results.

claims.statement: For an adult with mild traumatic brain injury who takes an anticoagulant, a usual clinical decision rule should not be used to exclude the need for head CT, and emergency imaging should be strongly considered.
claims.limitation: The authored cases use warfarin or direct oral anticoagulants and do not extend the teaching point to aspirin alone; the exact scan decision remains a clinical judgment in emergency care.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with mild traumatic brain injury who take warfarin or a direct oral anticoagulant.

claims.statement: In suspected pleural infection with nonpurulent aspirate, pleural-fluid pH at or below 7.2 indicates high risk and supports hospital intercostal drainage when ultrasound shows sufficient safely accessible fluid.
claims.limitation: The threshold requires the complete infection, sample, and ultrasound context; drainage is hospital care and evidence comes from one copyrighted guideline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected pleural infection and a nonpurulent diagnostic aspirate.

claims.statement: For a persistent esophageal foreign body requiring removal, therapeutic endoscopy is the initial approach when the supplied assessment has not identified a complication or circumstance requiring an operation.
claims.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy and surgical-indication sections directly support initial endoscopic care and separately identify operative indications. Sole direct source for this narrow comparator boundary. No extraction technique, universal avoidance of surgery, patient self-treatment or clinic procedure is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a confirmed retained esophageal foreign body and no supplied operative complication.

claims.statement: Some swallowed fish or chicken bones are not readily visible on plain radiographs, so a negative film does not exclude a retained bone.
claims.limitation: Direct concordant WSES 2019 imaging guidance and official ESGE 2016 PDF page 3. The older guidelines remain on current official indexes; underlying diagnostic evidence has limitations. No exact sensitivity, false-negative proportion, blanket plain-film-first rule or claim that every bone is radiolucent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic adults reporting swallowed fish or chicken bone.

claims.statement: A confirmed sharp-pointed foreign body retained in the esophagus is an indication for emergent therapeutic endoscopic removal.
claims.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy recommendation and ESGE 2016 official PDF page 4 agree. Strong guideline recommendations rely on largely low-quality evidence; age and current index status are recorded. The cases direct emergency hospital care outside the clinic, not a routine timed game EGD, a rescue protocol, extraction technique or a numeric deadline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with supplied confirmation of a sharp esophageal foreign body.

claims.statement: A sharp-pointed esophageal foreign body presents a risk of full-thickness esophageal injury, which underlies the need for emergent removal even without complete obstruction.
claims.limitation: Both guidelines support sharp-object urgency independent of the separate complete-obstruction indication. No exact perforation probability or claim that injury has already occurred. Cases have confirmed esophageal location, normal respiration and no supplied perforation; no onsite treatment or automatic surgery is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a confirmed retained sharp esophageal object and preserved breathing.

claims.statement: Absent Howell-Jolly bodies after splenectomy can support suspicion of residual functioning splenic tissue.
claims.limitation: Absence is supportive only; it is not independently diagnostic and is not sufficient to select surgery.
claims.applicablePopulation: Approved post-splenectomy hereditary-spherocytosis presentation with continued hemolysis.

claims.statement: Tc-99m heat-damaged RBC scintigraphy is the approved functional-tissue study for the constrained presentation after hereditary spherocytosis remains supported.
claims.limitation: The configured facility time is editorial game tuning rather than a clinical turnaround claim; this does not define a universal imaging sequence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients in the approved persistent-hemolysis functional-tissue evaluation presentation.

claims.statement: For the approved presentation of persistent anemia with biochemical hemolysis after documented total splenectomy, reassessment and evaluation for accessory splenic tissue is the selected next step.
claims.limitation: MCV or RDW alone does not establish persistent hemolysis, and this narrow teaching path does not diagnose every cause of anemia after splenectomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients matching the approved hereditary-spherocytosis post-splenectomy presentations.

claims.statement: For a stable patient with intermittent groin symptoms and an equivocal examination, targeted dynamic groin ultrasound is a selected next study to clarify possible inguinal hernia anatomy.
claims.limitation: Obvious hernias do not require routine imaging; ultrasound is operator-dependent, and a nondiagnostic study can require context-specific further imaging. NIDDK cites HerniaSurge, so it is not independent underlying trial evidence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable outpatients with activity-related groin symptoms, equivocal examination, and no incarceration, obstruction, or strangulation features.

claims.statement: Breastfeeding or expressed milk generally can continue from an affected breast when the infant's mouth and pump flange avoid purulent drainage, open infected tissue, and the drain site.
claims.limitation: Feeding safety remains individualized, including when an infant is immunocompromised or direct contact with infected tissue cannot be avoided.
claims.applicablePopulation: Lactating adults receiving care for a breast abscess whose infant and pump can avoid contact with purulent drainage, open tissue, and drains.

claims.statement: After a Lynch-suggestive tumor result, genetics counseling and germline-testing discussion are appropriate before assigning an inherited syndrome or family testing plan.
claims.limitation: MSH2/MSH6 loss can have germline, somatic, or EPCAM-related explanations; the case does not select a specific panel or result.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with colorectal-tumor IHC showing MSH2 and MSH6 loss with retained internal controls.

claims.statement: MMR IHC or MSI tumor testing can screen a newly diagnosed colorectal cancer for a possible Lynch-syndrome signal. Tumor screening is not germline testing and does not itself diagnose Lynch syndrome.
claims.limitation: Institutional pathways vary, and a screening result requires interpretation rather than a hereditary diagnosis.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with newly diagnosed colorectal cancer and no prior tumor MMR evaluation.

claims.statement: MEN2A includes medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism in the approved recognition scope.
claims.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata remains needs_clinician_review; exact question wording is separately approved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved MEN2A clinic variants.

claims.statement: A functioning pheochromocytoma must be excluded or addressed before thyroid intervention in the approved MEN2A scope.
claims.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata remains needs_clinician_review; exact question wording is separately approved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved MEN2A clinic variants.

claims.statement: Prosthetic mesh infection may present as a chronic or indolent deep process with sinus drainage, collection, fistula, or systemic infection rather than superficial incisional erythema alone.
claims.limitation: Single consensus source; findings require clinical correlation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults after hernia repair with implanted mesh.

claims.statement: Suspected deep mesh infection needs prompt specialist source-control evaluation; treatment is individualized and failed conservative management may require removal, so removal is not automatic.
claims.limitation: Exact antibiotics and operative technique are outside scope.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected deep prosthetic mesh infection.

claims.statement: When the gastrointestinal tract functions, oral intake and oral supplements are preferred first, with enteral nutrition used when oral intake is inadequate.
claims.limitation: Route choice remains individualized.
claims.applicablePopulation: Nutritionally at-risk adult surgical patients with a functional gastrointestinal tract.

claims.statement: Parenteral nutrition is reserved for situations in which oral and enteral routes are infeasible, contraindicated, or insufficient.
claims.limitation: No fixed timing, formulation, or dose is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult surgical patients needing nutrition support.

claims.statement: Resting ankle-brachial index testing is an appropriate initial physiologic test for reproducible exertional calf discomfort relieved by rest with examination findings suggesting lower-extremity peripheral arterial disease.
claims.limitation: Normal or high values can be misleading with noncompressible vessels; exercise ABI or toe-pressure assessment may be needed when suspicion persists.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with classic exertional calf symptoms, suggestive examination findings, and no limb threat.

claims.statement: Supervised exercise therapy or another structured exercise program is initial treatment for stable functionally limiting intermittent claudication before invasive revascularization when risk-reduction care is already addressed.
claims.limitation: This excludes ischemic rest pain, tissue loss, acute ischemia, and ongoing limb threat and does not prescribe a universal duration or medication regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with functionally limiting intermittent claudication and no limb-threatening ischemia.

claims.statement: A specialist-performed local-anesthetic trigger-point or peripheral nerve block may add diagnostic information, but evidence is very low and no technique or response is guaranteed.
claims.limitation: External specialist assessment only; no treatment ladder or guaranteed response.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with persistent focal pain after recurrence and other causes are reassessed.

claims.statement: Persistent pain after inguinal-hernia repair requires focused history and examination, pain mapping, and reassessment for recurrence and other causes; a compatible neuropathic distribution supports but does not alone prove a nerve mechanism.
claims.limitation: No single symptom proves a named nerve lesion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with persistent pain after inguinal-hernia repair.

claims.statement: Initial hospital management of large, symptomatic, reaccumulating postoperative chylous ascites can include symptom-directed peritoneal drainage, restriction of long-chain triglycerides with medium-chain triglyceride enrichment, and monitoring of nutrition, fluid, and electrolytes.
claims.limitation: Evidence is heterogeneous, drainage is symptom- and accumulation-dependent, and persistent or severe refractory leakage may require individualized lymphatic localization, intervention, or surgery. This claim does not impose a rigid escalation timeline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable postoperative adults with confirmed large, symptomatic, reaccumulating chylous ascites.

claims.statement: Parenteral nutrition supplies nutrients while oral and enteral feeding are infeasible; it does not directly restore bowel motility, replace evaluation for obstruction, or prevent resumption of enteral feeding when gastrointestinal function returns.
claims.limitation: Ongoing ileus management and reassessment are outside this single nutritional-support concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults receiving parenteral nutrition because prolonged postoperative ileus prevents adequate oral or enteral feeding.

claims.statement: PTLD is heterogeneous; in a solid-organ recipient, unexplained fever, lymphadenopathy, an extranodal mass, organ dysfunction, or rising EBV viremia should prompt evaluation while infection and rejection remain mimics.
claims.limitation: The list is nonexhaustive and no one feature establishes PTLD.
claims.applicablePopulation: Solid-organ transplant recipients with otherwise unexplained concerning findings.

claims.statement: Tissue pathology is required to diagnose and classify suspected PTLD; EBV DNA and imaging are supportive and do not replace histopathologic diagnosis.
claims.limitation: No biopsy technique, staging system, surveillance cutoff, or treatment regimen is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Transplant recipients with suspected PTLD.

claims.statement: Local response assessment after neoadjuvant treatment for rectal cancer combines digital rectal examination, endoscopic examination, and rectal-protocol MRI.
claims.limitation: Biopsy alone cannot establish complete response, and this pathway assumes systemic imaging has already excluded metastases.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with known mid or low rectal cancer after completed neoadjuvant treatment.

claims.statement: For a fully informed patient with a clinical complete response who prefers nonsurgical care and can adhere to intensive follow-up in an experienced multidisciplinary program, watch-and-wait is a reasonable option.
claims.limitation: This is a conditional option, not proof of pathological cure or mandatory care; total mesorectal excision remains a valid alternative and surveillance must be intensive.
claims.applicablePopulation: Selected adherent adults with a clinical complete response after neoadjuvant rectal cancer treatment and access to an experienced program.

claims.statement: A mechanical transition pattern does not by itself establish or exclude bowel ischemia; clinical and additional CT danger features determine concern.
claims.limitation: No single omitted sign is used to declare bowel viability.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with CT evidence of SBO.

claims.statement: A completed CT showing proximal small-bowel dilation, a transition point, and distal decompression supports mechanical SBO.
claims.limitation: CT interpretation must be integrated with clinical assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected mechanical SBO and completed CT imaging.

claims.statement: Conservative care remains reasonable when preference, comorbidity, mobility, anatomy, or resources weigh against intervention.
claims.limitation: No universal garment or duration is prescribed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with stable symptomatic varicose veins.

claims.statement: For symptomatic axial superficial reflux in an intervention candidate who wants treatment, specialist superficial venous intervention assessment is preferred to mandatory long-term compression.
claims.limitation: The exact procedure depends on specialist anatomy and assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with symptomatic axial superficial reflux who are intervention candidates.

claims.statement: Arterial status should be assessed before selecting compression for a suspected venous leg ulcer because coexisting arterial disease changes compression safety and type.
claims.limitation: ABI can be unreliable with noncompressible arteries and this teaching does not prescribe a numeric cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a suspected venous leg ulcer and no acute limb ischemia.

claims.statement: Contrast swallow with fluoroscopy is an appropriate first anatomic test when cervical dysphagia and regurgitation of retained food specifically suggest a proximal pharyngoesophageal pouch.
claims.limitation: This does not generalize to all persistent esophageal dysphagia, for which endoscopy often leads after oropharyngeal disease is excluded.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a classic presentation suggesting a proximal pharyngoesophageal pouch.

claims.statement: A posterior pouch containing mucosa and submucosa above the cricopharyngeus supports Zenker diverticulum and reflects impaired cricopharyngeal opening with increased pharyngeal pressure.
claims.limitation: A lateral pouch below the cricopharyngeus suggests another diverticulum; returned imaging supports the pattern without selecting a treatment technique.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with returned contrast-swallow anatomy showing a posterior pouch above the cricopharyngeus.

claims.statement: A localized superficial incisional surgical-site infection with purulence requires opening the involved incision and drainage, with removal of sutures or staples when needed for source control.
claims.limitation: Systemic antibiotics depend on systemic response and operative site; deep, organ-space, and necrotizing infections require different care.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with purulent superficial incisional infection, intact fascia, and no systemic toxicity.

claims.statement: A stable adult with an adrenal incidentaloma at least 1 cm should undergo biochemical evaluation for autonomous cortisol secretion with a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test.
claims.limitation: Testing may be unwarranted in frail patients with limited life expectancy. An abnormal result requires contextual interpretation and does not by itself mandate adrenalectomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable, nonfrail adults with an incidentally discovered adrenal mass at least 1 cm.

claims.statement: After duplex suggests severe stenosis in a patient with a recent ipsilateral retinal or hemispheric ischemic event, CTA or MRA is used to confirm stenosis and define anatomy before revascularization planning.
claims.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. CTA and MRA selection is individualized; this pathway uses CTA and assumes the acute stroke assessment is complete.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults after completed acute assessment for a resolved ipsilateral retinal or nondisabling hemispheric ischemic event.

claims.statement: A lesion suspected to be cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma should have biopsy adequate for diagnosis and risk assessment; the selected technique depends on lesion features and location.
claims.limitation: This does not require one biopsy technique for every lesion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a suspicious keratotic skin lesion and no tissue diagnosis.

claims.statement: Severe infection or moderate infection with important morbidity warrants hospital consideration; gangrene, deep abscess, necrotizing infection, compartment syndrome, or severe ischemia warrants urgent surgical consultation.
claims.limitation: The clinic objective stops at recognition and external escalation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with diabetes-related foot infection and danger features.

claims.statement: After recovery, elective sigmoid-resection discussion should use complications, ongoing burden, operative risk, and patient preferences rather than a simple episode count.
claims.limitation: A shared discussion is not a mandatory operation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable recovered diverticulitis patients considering elective surgery.

claims.statement: Upper-GI endoscopy with appropriate esophageal biopsies evaluates persistent esophageal dysphagia by examining mucosa and structural narrowing and obtaining tissue when indicated.
claims.limitation: This does not prescribe an emergency pathway, universal dilation, screening criteria, or a test sequence for every dysphagia presentation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent esophageal dysphagia who can tolerate liquids and have no acute food impaction.

claims.statement: MRI can be selected to map recurrent or complex anal fistula anatomy before a treatment plan.
claims.limitation: Imaging is not presented as routine for simple fistula.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with recurrent or complex fistula features.

claims.statement: Gastroparesis is diagnosed in a patient with compatible upper gastrointestinal symptoms by documenting objectively delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claims.limitation: Compatible symptoms alone are not diagnostic, and this concept assumes that an appropriate prior evaluation has already excluded mechanical obstruction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with chronic nausea, vomiting, early satiety, or postprandial fullness and no demonstrated mechanical gastric-outlet obstruction.

claims.statement: Cross-sectional imaging can demonstrate and localize ascites but cannot by appearance alone establish that the fluid is chylous.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with postoperative intraperitoneal fluid under evaluation for possible chylous ascites.

claims.statement: Suspected postoperative chylous ascites requires diagnostic fluid sampling with triglyceride measurement and studies directed at infection and other plausible postoperative leaks rather than diagnosis from imaging appearance alone.
claims.limitation: The exact ancillary fluid studies depend on the operation and differential diagnosis. This approved concept does not teach an unsourced universal numeric triglyceride cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults with newly identified ascites and suspected lymphatic leakage.

claims.statement: Initial hospital management of large, symptomatic, reaccumulating postoperative chylous ascites can include symptom-directed peritoneal drainage, restriction of long-chain triglycerides with medium-chain triglyceride enrichment, and monitoring of nutrition, fluid, and electrolytes.
claims.limitation: Evidence is heterogeneous, drainage is symptom- and accumulation-dependent, and persistent or severe refractory leakage may require individualized lymphatic localization, intervention, or surgery. This claim does not impose a rigid escalation timeline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable postoperative adults with confirmed large, symptomatic, reaccumulating chylous ascites.

claims.statement: Vitamin C, or ascorbate, is a required cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase activity during collagen biosynthesis.

claims.applicablePopulation: General human collagen biosynthesis and perioperative wound-healing education.

claims.statement: Inadequate vitamin C impairs proline and lysine hydroxylation, compromising normal collagen maturation and stability and contributing to impaired wound healing.
claims.limitation: This mechanism does not establish that vitamin C deficiency is the cause of every impaired wound or that supplementation improves healing in every patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: General human collagen biosynthesis and perioperative wound-healing education.

claims.statement: The established biochemical requirement for vitamin C does not by itself justify routine high-dose supplementation as a universal treatment for every well-nourished postoperative patient.
claims.limitation: Clinical supplementation evidence varies across populations and wound types; this concept teaches mechanism and does not prescribe a dose or treatment protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Postoperative patients without a separately established vitamin C deficiency or condition-specific supplementation indication.

claims.statement: Gastric MALT lymphoma is recognized by an integrated pathologic pattern that includes a small B-cell infiltrate with gland-infiltrating lymphoepithelial lesions and a compatible immunophenotype, commonly CD20 positive with CD5, CD10, and cyclin D1 absent.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing pathologic evaluation of a gastric lymphoid infiltrate obtained by endoscopic biopsy.

claims.statement: For confirmed localized low-grade gastric MALT lymphoma associated with H. pylori and without large-cell transformation or another adverse presentation, H. pylori eradication is appropriate initial lymphoma-directed treatment without concurrent gastrectomy, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy.
claims.limitation: The exact eradication regimen depends on current local resistance patterns, allergies, prior antibiotic exposure, and applicable H. pylori guidance; this concept does not prescribe a regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed localized low-grade H. pylori-positive gastric MALT lymphoma without transformation or immediately threatening disease.

claims.statement: Initial eradication treatment must be followed by confirmation that H. pylori was eradicated and by endoscopic biopsy reassessment of lymphoma response rather than being treated as a one-time antibiotic prescription with no follow-up.
claims.limitation: Lymphoma regression can be delayed. Exact follow-up intervals and subsequent management depend on eradication status, pathology, symptoms, stage, and adverse features.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for gastric MALT lymphoma.

claims.statement: Large-cell transformation, clinically significant progression, threatening organ effects, or failure after an adequate eradication pathway requires reassessment and may require radiotherapy or systemic lymphoma treatment rather than repetition of an eradication-only strategy.
claims.limitation: This boundary does not assign one universal second-line treatment; subsequent therapy is individualized to stage, pathology, symptoms, prior response, and specialist assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastric MALT lymphoma outside the classic localized low-grade eradication-first presentation or with an inadequate response.

claims.statement: Gastroparesis is diagnosed in a patient with compatible upper gastrointestinal symptoms by documenting objectively delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claims.limitation: Compatible symptoms alone are not diagnostic, and this concept assumes that an appropriate prior evaluation has already excluded mechanical obstruction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with chronic nausea, vomiting, early satiety, or postprandial fullness and no demonstrated mechanical gastric-outlet obstruction.

claims.statement: Four-hour solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy is the preferred objective study in this concept for suspected gastroparesis after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claims.limitation: The 2022 ACG guideline recommends solid-meal scintigraphy for at least three hours, while the 2025 AGA guideline specifically favors four-hour testing over studies lasting two hours or less. This concept does not teach an exact abnormal-retention cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing objective evaluation for suspected gastroparesis after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.

claims.statement: Upper endoscopy can help exclude mechanical obstruction but does not replace objective gastric emptying measurement; esophageal manometry and ambulatory pH monitoring evaluate different physiologic questions.
claims.limitation: Other validated gastric-emptying modalities may have selected roles. They are not taught or used as false distractors in this narrowly approved scintigraphic-testing concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing outpatient evaluation for suspected gastroparesis.

claims.statement: The approved prolonged postoperative-ileus presentation requires persistent severe gastrointestinal dysfunction beyond seven postoperative days, exclusion of mechanical obstruction or another precipitating diagnosis, and inability to tolerate adequate oral or enteral nutrition.
claims.limitation: A postoperative-day number or high nasogastric output alone is insufficient. Nutritional status, likely duration, reversible contributors, and oral or enteral feasibility remain clinically important.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults with prolonged severe postoperative ileus after major abdominal surgery.

claims.statement: Parenteral nutrition is appropriate nutritional support in the approved presentation when prolonged postoperative ileus prevents adequate oral or enteral nutrition beyond seven days and mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claims.limitation: This scope does not establish a universal instruction to delay nutrition until day seven. Malnutrition, high metabolic risk, critical illness, expected duration, and partial enteral tolerance can change timing and whether supplemental or total parenteral nutrition is used.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults with persistent severe postoperative ileus who cannot use the gastrointestinal route for adequate nutrition.

claims.statement: Parenteral nutrition supplies nutrients while oral and enteral feeding are infeasible; it does not directly restore bowel motility, replace evaluation for obstruction, or prevent resumption of enteral feeding when gastrointestinal function returns.
claims.limitation: Ongoing ileus management and reassessment are outside this single nutritional-support concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults receiving parenteral nutrition because prolonged postoperative ileus prevents adequate oral or enteral feeding.

claims.statement: Routine prophylactic splenectomy does not improve survival during curative gastrectomy for resectable proximal gastric adenocarcinoma without greater-curvature invasion, direct splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.
claims.limitation: This claim applies to prophylactic splenectomy in the defined proximal-gastric-cancer population and must not be generalized to every gastric tumor or to a therapeutic splenectomy indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing curative resection for proximal gastric adenocarcinoma without greater-curvature invasion, splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.

claims.statement: In the approved population, adding prophylactic splenectomy increases operative morbidity while spleen preservation maintains oncologic survival.
claims.limitation: The package does not teach exact complication rates or substitute this population-level result for individualized operative planning.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the approved proximal-gastric-cancer operative population.

claims.statement: The spleen-preservation teaching point is not a rule that splenectomy is never appropriate; direct splenic invasion, greater-curvature invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease falls outside the approved routine-prophylaxis scenario.
claims.limitation: Falling outside this scope does not by itself prescribe splenectomy; the specific operative decision remains separately authored clinical content.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for curative proximal gastric-cancer surgery.

claims.statement: For an extensively burned patient who has been adequately resuscitated and has no enteral contraindication, enteral nutrition should begin as soon as feasible within the first 24 hours after injury.
claims.limitation: The evidence supports early feeding but does not establish eight hours as a universal cutoff. The exact start depends on resuscitation, hemodynamic status, access, contraindications, and clinical feasibility.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with extensive burns who are adequately resuscitated, hemodynamically stable, unable to meet nutritional needs orally, and without a contraindication to enteral nutrition.

claims.statement: When the gastrointestinal tract is usable, enteral nutrition is the preferred initial route for nutritional support after an extensive burn rather than routine first-line parenteral nutrition.
claims.limitation: This claim does not prescribe a feeding-access site, formula, advancement protocol, or management plan when adequate enteral nutrition is infeasible or contraindicated.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with extensive burns who require nutritional support and have a usable gastrointestinal tract.

claims.statement: The approved early-enteral-nutrition rule requires adequate resuscitation and no enteral contraindication; ongoing shock, incomplete resuscitation, suspected intestinal ischemia, or mechanical obstruction falls outside this teaching scenario.
claims.limitation: Falling outside the approved scenario does not itself specify parenteral nutrition or another intervention; those decisions require separately authored clinical content.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with extensive burns being assessed for initiation of enteral nutritional support.

claims.statement: In a stable adult undergoing ventral or incisional hernia repair, a recognized small-bowel enterotomy that has been securely repaired with adequate source control, minimal controlled contamination, and no ongoing gross spillage does not automatically preclude a selected single-stage mesh repair.
claims.limitation: Direct evidence for an inadvertent enterotomy during elective repair remains limited. Whether to continue, convert, or defer repair requires individualized judgment; this approved concept begins only after the team has determined that single-stage repair is appropriate.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults undergoing ventral or incisional hernia repair after immediate recognition and secure repair of a small-bowel enterotomy with controlled contamination and no gross spillage.

claims.statement: When a selected single-stage ventral or incisional hernia repair proceeds after controlled enterotomy, permanent macroporous monofilament synthetic mesh is preferred over defaulting to biologic, microporous multifilament, or rapidly absorbable mesh solely because the field is clean-contaminated.
claims.limitation: The randomized trial addresses elective clean-contaminated and contaminated repairs rather than the exact inadvertent-enterotomy scenario, and the current EHS recommendation is conditional with low to very-low evidence certainty. Mesh plane, fixation, and direct bowel contact are not addressed by this concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Selected stable adults proceeding with single-stage ventral or incisional hernia repair after adequate source control in a minimally contaminated field.

claims.statement: Unstable physiology, uncertain bowel viability, an unrecognized or delayed enterotomy, incomplete source control, or persistent gross enteric or feculent spillage falls outside the approved macroporous-synthetic-mesh selection rule.
claims.limitation: Falling outside this scope does not by itself prescribe tissue repair, biologic mesh, staged reconstruction, or abandonment; those operative decisions require separately authored content.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with an enterotomy or gastrointestinal contamination encountered during ventral or incisional hernia repair.

claims.statement: A right thoracotomy directly exposes the proximal or middle intrathoracic esophagus, intrathoracic trachea, and azygos vein and can therefore address selected combinations of localized injuries to those structures.
claims.limitation: Exposure is not equivalent to a universal operative recommendation. Hemodynamic state, exact injury level, trajectory, associated injuries, pleural contamination, and need for vascular or cardiac control may require a different or extended incision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Trauma patients with localized intrathoracic injuries undergoing operative exposure selection after initial assessment.

claims.statement: For a sufficiently stable trauma patient undergoing planned open repair of a localized upper or middle thoracic esophageal injury, a right posterolateral thoracotomy is an appropriate exposure; selected associated azygos or intrathoracic tracheal injuries can reinforce the right-sided choice.
claims.limitation: This claim assumes that the injury is localized and the patient can undergo a planned definitive exposure. Distal esophageal injuries are generally approached from the left, and the side of major pleural contamination or a competing cardiac or great-vessel injury can change the incision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable or stabilized trauma patients with a localized upper or middle thoracic esophageal injury selected for planned open repair.

claims.statement: A planned right posterolateral thoracotomy is not the default incision for a patient in traumatic arrest or extremis who requires immediate resuscitative chest access; resuscitative access is generally anterior and may require left anterolateral or clamshell exposure according to the suspected injury and local protocol.
claims.limitation: This boundary does not define eligibility for resuscitative thoracotomy or prescribe one incision for every arrest scenario. Those indications and technique choices require separate content.
claims.applicablePopulation: Trauma patients being assessed for immediate resuscitative versus planned definitive thoracic exposure.

claims.statement: For a symptomatic Meckel diverticulum, inflammation or disruption involving the diverticular base and adjacent ileum favors bowel-inclusive resection over simple diverticulectomy; segmental ileal resection is appropriate when adjacent ileum is involved.
claims.limitation: Wedge and segmental resection can both be reasonable in selected base-involved cases. The approved segmental-resection variants therefore specify adjacent ileal involvement rather than using base width alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adolescent or adult patients with a symptomatic Meckel diverticulum identified during abdominal exploration.

claims.statement: Simple diverticulectomy is an appropriate resection for a long, narrow Meckel diverticulum when uncomplicated inflammation is confined to the distal tip and the base and adjacent ileum are healthy.
claims.limitation: Macroscopic morphology does not perfectly predict heterotopic tissue. This claim does not extend to bleeding, tumor, obstruction, base perforation, or adjacent ileal disease.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adolescent or adult patients with a symptomatic long, narrow Meckel diverticulum and inflammation confined to the distal tip.

claims.statement: One retrospective series of 15 adults with perforated Meckel diverticula operationally classified a base width of 2 cm or greater as broad and less than 2 cm as narrow.
claims.limitation: This is a source-specific operational definition from a small perforation series, not a validated universal cutoff and not an independent indication for segmental resection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with perforated Meckel diverticulum in the cited retrospective series.

claims.statement: No exact base-width measurement should be treated as a universal stand-alone rule for Meckel resection extent; disease location and the integrity of the base and adjacent ileum remain necessary operative context.
claims.limitation: Morphology studies are retrospective and partly conflicting. Diverticulum length greater than 2 cm is a separate observation about symptomatic risk and must not be confused with a 2 cm base-width definition.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with a Meckel diverticulum undergoing operative assessment.

claims.statement: Contemporary pooled and national-registry evidence reports higher observed perioperative mortality among women than men after elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.
claims.limitation: The evidence is derived primarily from observational cohorts and pooled observational estimates; it supports an association rather than a causal or patient-specific prediction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm; the approved concept is limited to counseling about population-level perioperative outcomes.

claims.statement: Higher observed perioperative mortality among women has been reported after both endovascular and open elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.
claims.limitation: Effect estimates and contributing mechanisms vary across cohorts, anatomy, repair approach, era, and adjustment methods; the claim does not compare an individual patient's suitability for EVAR versus open repair.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving elective EVAR or open repair for intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.

claims.statement: A sex-associated difference in population-level operative outcomes informs counseling and risk assessment but does not determine an individual patient's outcome or make female sex a contraindication to repair.
claims.limitation: Individual risk still depends on anatomy, comorbidity, repair approach, center experience, and other patient-specific factors not taught by this concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Learners interpreting observed sex-associated AAA repair outcomes during counseling without converting the association into deterministic treatment advice.

claims.statement: The 2022 ACC/AHA guideline recommends elective repair of an unruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm at a maximum diameter of at least 5.5 cm in men or at least 5.0 cm in women, and trials of routine repair for smaller asymptomatic aneurysms did not demonstrate a survival benefit.
claims.limitation: Diameter is not the only management consideration; symptoms, growth, anatomy, operative risk, patient preference, and specialist assessment remain relevant. This claim is used only to bound distractors in the approved concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with unruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm being evaluated for surveillance or elective repair.

claims.statement: Active surveillance through an experienced multidisciplinary team is an appropriate initial strategy for many newly diagnosed desmoid tumors that are stable, minimally symptomatic, and not threatening a critical structure or meaningful function.
claims.limitation: Surveillance is an active specialist-management strategy, not absence of follow-up; this concept does not specify a universal imaging interval or apply to persistent progression, critical-site threat, obstruction, or meaningful functional decline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with biopsy-confirmed, newly diagnosed desmoid tumor without persistent progression, critical-site threat, obstruction, or meaningful functional deterioration.

claims.statement: Active treatment may be considered after persistent radiologic or clinical progression or when desmoid disease threatens a critical structure or meaningful function.
claims.limitation: The choice of active treatment is individualized by location, tempo, symptoms, expected morbidity, patient goals, and specialist review; progression does not make one treatment universal.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with desmoid tumor demonstrating persistent progression, critical-site threat, pain, obstruction, or meaningful functional deterioration.

claims.statement: After multidisciplinary review, surgery can be proposed for a progressing, symptomatic, resectable abdominal-wall desmoid when expected morbidity is acceptably low.
claims.limitation: This location-specific option does not make surgery mandatory and should not be generalized to mesenteric, head-and-neck, chest-wall, extremity, or other disease where medical or other local treatment may better preserve function.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with persistently progressing abdominal-wall desmoid tumor causing meaningful pain or functional limitation and an acceptably low expected morbidity from resection.

claims.statement: When surgery is selected for desmoid tumor, preservation of function and cosmesis may justify accepting a microscopically positive margin rather than pursuing a wider resection with avoidable morbidity.
claims.limitation: This is not permission to perform an unplanned incomplete operation; operative goals and acceptable morbidity require specialist multidisciplinary planning.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients selected for desmoid resection when a wider microscopic margin would cause avoidable functional or cosmetic harm.

claims.statement: Desmoid tumors may grow infiltratively and recur locally but do not metastasize; symptoms or progression do not convert them into metastatic malignancies.
claims.limitation: Lack of metastatic potential does not make locally progressive or critical-site disease harmless.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with pathologically confirmed desmoid-type fibromatosis.

claims.statement: Peptic ulcers with active spurting, active oozing, or a nonbleeding visible vessel are high-risk endoscopic findings for which endoscopic hemostasis is indicated.
claims.limitation: This claim assumes the patient has been appropriately assessed and stabilized for endoscopy; it does not define pre-endoscopy resuscitation, transfusion, medication, or disposition decisions.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing upper endoscopy for suspected or confirmed nonvariceal peptic-ulcer bleeding.

claims.statement: A clean-based peptic ulcer or a flat pigmented spot does not require endoscopic hemostatic treatment solely for that stigma.
claims.limitation: The absence of an endoscopic hemostasis indication does not determine the complete medical treatment, cause-specific therapy, observation need, or discharge plan.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults whose upper endoscopy shows a peptic ulcer with a clean base or flat pigmented spot and no separate high-risk bleeding stigma.

claims.statement: A nonbleeding visible vessel may be treated with an accepted thermal or mechanical hemostatic modality as monotherapy, or with such a definitive modality combined with epinephrine injection.
claims.limitation: The concept does not claim that every available modality is equivalent in every lesion, that two definitive modalities are routinely required, or that device selection is independent of anatomy, expertise, and equipment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a peptic ulcer containing a nonbleeding visible vessel during upper endoscopy.

claims.statement: Epinephrine injection should not be used as the sole definitive endoscopic treatment for a high-risk bleeding peptic ulcer; when epinephrine is selected, it must be paired with a definitive hemostatic modality.
claims.limitation: This claim does not require epinephrine in every hemostatic plan and does not make an accepted thermal, mechanical, or selected advanced modality inadequate merely because injection was omitted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving endoscopic hemostasis for a peptic ulcer with active bleeding or a nonbleeding visible vessel when epinephrine injection is under consideration.

claims.statement: A conventional combination pathway for an actively bleeding peptic ulcer uses dilute epinephrine injection for temporary control followed by contact thermal or mechanical hemostasis.
claims.limitation: This is a conventional pathway, not a claim that every actively bleeding ulcer must receive epinephrine or that selected contemporary OTS-clip or hemostatic-forceps monotherapy is never appropriate.
claims.applicablePopulation: Appropriately stabilized adults undergoing hospital endoscopy for an actively bleeding peptic ulcer when the conventional epinephrine-combination pathway is selected.

claims.statement: Current guidance recognizes selected advanced monotherapy options, including over-the-scope clipping for certain high-risk actively bleeding ulcers and hemostatic forceps with soft coagulation, so generic clip or cautery monotherapy cannot be labeled universally wrong.
claims.limitation: The exact choice depends on lesion characteristics, device type, technical competence, local resources, and recommendation strength; these advanced options are boundaries for distractor authoring rather than scored content in this package.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing expert endoscopic hemostasis for high-risk peptic-ulcer bleeding.

claims.statement: PDSA is an iterative learning method: teams test a change on a limited scale, study what happened, refine the change, and use linked cycles to build toward broader implementation when results support it.
claims.limitation: This claim does not establish the appropriate aim, measures, sample size, duration, or implementation threshold for a particular project.
claims.applicablePopulation: Healthcare teams conducting structured quality-improvement tests, including ambulatory-surgery teams.

claims.statement: After studying a test's results, the Act step uses those findings to adopt, adapt, or abandon the tested change and to prepare the next test as appropriate.
claims.limitation: The three labels summarize a decision framework; the specific decision still depends on the project's prespecified aim, results, balancing measures, and operational context.
claims.applicablePopulation: Healthcare teams that have completed and studied a limited quality-improvement test.

claims.statement: The next quality-improvement action should follow the observed results: expand a successful change cautiously, revise and retest a partially successful change, or stop or redesign an unsuccessful change rather than switching methods or continuing unchanged automatically.
claims.limitation: Root-cause analysis or another improvement framework may be useful for a separately defined problem; this claim only rejects their automatic use solely because a PDSA test has reached the Act step.
claims.applicablePopulation: Healthcare quality-improvement teams choosing a next action after reviewing a completed test of change.

claims.statement: When operative resection is selected for resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the body or tail, the anatomic pancreatic resection is a distal pancreatectomy rather than a pancreaticoduodenectomy.
claims.limitation: This location-based operation does not determine treatment sequencing or establish resectability by itself.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the pancreatic body or tail who are selected to proceed with operative resection.

claims.statement: Standard oncologic distal resection for pancreatic body or tail adenocarcinoma includes splenectomy as part of distal pancreatectomy and regional oncologic clearance.
claims.limitation: This approved teaching point is specific to confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma and does not define the operation for benign distal lesions, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, trauma, or other non-adenocarcinoma indications.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the body or tail who are selected for oncologic resection.

claims.statement: Absence of distant metastases is necessary but not sufficient to select pancreatic-cancer surgery; anatomic resectability, operative fitness, disease biology, and multidisciplinary treatment planning also matter.
claims.limitation: The approved variants state that the tumor has already been judged resectable and ask which operation or referral follows if surgery proceeds; they do not choose neoadjuvant versus upfront treatment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary evaluation for potentially resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

claims.statement: Pancreaticoduodenectomy is used for pancreatic head or uncinate cancer, while distal pancreatectomy is used for pancreatic body or tail cancer; total pancreatectomy is not required solely because a resectable cancer is in the tail.
claims.limitation: Multifocal or locally extensive disease can create separate indications for total pancreatectomy, but those scenarios are outside this concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma being considered for resection.

claims.statement: Felty syndrome is suggested by long-standing, usually seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with persistent neutropenia; splenomegaly is a characteristic supporting feature and recurrent infections may be the presenting problem.
claims.limitation: The pattern is not pathognomonic. The approved diagnostic vignette explicitly excludes medication, infection, and clonal large-granular-lymphocyte causes before asking for the syndrome.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with established rheumatoid arthritis and persistent otherwise-unexplained neutropenia.

claims.statement: Splenomegaly is common in Felty syndrome but is not an absolute prerequisite; persistent neutropenia in the appropriate rheumatoid-arthritis context remains the essential hematologic feature.
claims.limitation: A normal-sized spleen does not establish Felty syndrome and does not remove the need to investigate alternative causes of neutropenia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with rheumatoid arthritis and persistent neutropenia after alternative causes have been evaluated.

claims.statement: T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia and other hematologic, infectious, autoimmune, and medication-related causes can resemble Felty syndrome and require explicit exclusion rather than diagnosis from the triad alone.
claims.limitation: This package does not teach the complete hematologic workup or a separate T-LGL diagnosis concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with rheumatoid arthritis, neutropenia, and possible splenomegaly undergoing diagnostic evaluation.

claims.statement: Methotrexate is the usual first-line disease-modifying treatment for confirmed Felty syndrome when treatment is indicated, with specialist monitoring of blood counts and clinical response.
claims.limitation: Felty syndrome is rare and treatment evidence is based mainly on case reports and small case series rather than randomized trials; this concept does not prescribe a dose or monitoring interval.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed Felty syndrome who do not have an active infection and have not yet received syndrome-directed disease-modifying treatment.

claims.statement: Glucocorticoids or G-CSF may be used as temporary bridging or supportive therapy while disease-modifying treatment takes effect; glucocorticoids are not universally contraindicated but should be avoided in active infection and are not the preferred sole long-term strategy.
claims.limitation: The approved questions do not prescribe a dose, duration, laboratory target, or universal bridging regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed Felty syndrome receiving specialist-directed treatment.

claims.statement: Splenectomy is generally reserved for Felty syndrome with recurrent infections despite adequate medical treatment rather than used as routine initial therapy.
claims.limitation: The exact likelihood and durability of hematologic response are not taught because the evidence is old, heterogeneous, and confounded by historical overlap with T-LGL leukemia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed Felty syndrome and recurrent infections despite adequate specialist-directed medical therapy.

claims.statement: For benign phyllodes tumors, complete excision is the counseling target without a prescribed fixed-width margin.
claims.limitation: Management wording is evidence-sensitive consensus guidance and does not establish a universal biological cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with pathology-confirmed benign phyllodes tumors considering local treatment.

claims.statement: A positive margin after benign phyllodes excision does not by itself require re-excision; residual or transected-tumor concern changes the discussion.
claims.limitation: This is counseling guidance, not a substitute for individualized pathology and multidisciplinary review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with benign phyllodes tumors after complete excision and a positive margin.

claims.statement: Borderline phyllodes counseling uses a 5-mm margin aim for complete excision planning.
claims.limitation: The margin aim is consensus management guidance with evidence limitations, not a biological cliff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with borderline phyllodes tumors undergoing local treatment planning.

claims.statement: For borderline phyllodes, a margin below 3 mm supports re-excision and a 3-to-under-5-mm margin supports individualized re-excision discussion.
claims.limitation: Intervals are evidence-sensitive consensus management boundaries rather than universal biological cutoffs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with borderline phyllodes tumors after excision with a close margin.

claims.statement: Malignant phyllodes counseling uses a 10-mm margin aim for complete excision planning.
claims.limitation: The margin aim is consensus management guidance with evidence limitations, not a biological cliff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with malignant phyllodes tumors undergoing local treatment planning.

claims.statement: For malignant phyllodes, a margin below 5 mm supports re-excision; at 5 to under 10 mm, re-excision is recommended while surveillance may be considered only after explicit risk-benefit discussion.
claims.limitation: Intervals are evidence-sensitive consensus management boundaries rather than universal biological cutoffs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with malignant phyllodes tumors after excision with a close margin.

claims.statement: Phyllodes tumors have a predominantly hematogenous metastatic pattern, with nodal spread uncommon relative to hematogenous spread.
claims.limitation: This describes a usual pattern and does not predict the course for an individual patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients receiving counseling about malignant phyllodes tumor spread patterns.

claims.statement: Routine sentinel-node or axillary staging is not indicated for phyllodes tumors when axillary nodes are nonsuspicious.
claims.limitation: This boundary applies to nonsuspicious nodes and does not replace evaluation of a concerning axillary finding.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with benign, borderline, or malignant phyllodes tumors and nonsuspicious axillary nodes.

claims.statement: A suspicious axillary node in a patient with phyllodes history warrants image-guided histopathologic needle biopsy; biopsy-proven involvement may prompt axillary-dissection consideration after MDT discussion.
claims.limitation: This exception is driven by the suspicious-node evaluation and requires individualized multidisciplinary review.
